title: Aaron Burr, autograph letter 'largely in cypher' to James Wilkinson (Newberry copy), with Wilkinson's explanation of the cypher filed separately
shelfmark: Newberry Library, Case MS 7A 4 (Graff f*502 in Cusk's checklist of English manuscripts)
folio_note: one autograph letter, unsigned, largely in cypher; extent not stated
status: Cusk checklist: 'Autograph letter, unsigned, largely in cypher, addressed to James Wilkinson', 1806, Burr Conspiracy. Newberry also holds Wilkinson's memorandum 'explanation of the cypher used in the Burr-Wilkinson correspondence' (VAULT folio Graff 4668, digitised, nby_graff/16326). The famous 22 July 1806 Burr cipher letter was deciphered and printed at the 1807 trial, so this is probably a copy, duplicate or variant of a known letter; not confirmed. Not on DECODE (not searched by shelfmark); known.py: no hit for Newberry/Case MS 7A 4. Repo has related Wilkinson and Graham 1806 entries (catalogue 482, 761) but not this item.
why: A second surviving copy or a variant of Burr's conspiracy cipher letter, with the contemporary key explanation held beside it, could settle which version Wilkinson actually received.
verify: Ask the Newberry for images of Case MS 7A 4; compare with the printed cipher letter of 22 July 1806 (Trial of Aaron Burr, 1807; Jackson/Founders edition) and with the digitised Graff 4668 key explanation.
prior_art: open as to this copy (checked 28 Oct 2026: Newberry catalogue, Cusk checklist, repo known.py; the 22 July 1806 letter itself is published, not re-checked in full)

status: Catalogue record note: 'Some sections appear to be in shorthand or code. Tipped in: 1 folded leaf containing note in shorthand or code.' No decipherment noted; may be shorthand rather than cipher. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit.
why: A private code or shorthand in a mid-19th-century Philippines notebook; low historical weight unless it hides the compiler's identity or sources.

title: Case MS 5017 occult manuscript (17th c.), folio with a characters table and two sample lines 'in cipher'
correspondents: unknown (compiler not identified; not verified to be Robert Ashley)
shelfmark: Newberry Library, Case MS 5017 (digital item case_ms_5017_020_o2, CONTENTdm nby_dig/2714)
folio_note: one page: table of symbols paired with letters, with two sample ciphertexts transcribed in the image alt-text as 'edward; eliet' and 'writ; tsis'
status: Digitised page: 'This Table which standeth here underneth serveth them who are desirous to use a form of Characters to write in that maner that no man shall reade; but by the Table folowing.' The page carries its own key, so the examples are readable. This is a key lead, not an unsolved text; the other pages (case_ms_5017_070_o2 matched 'code') may hold further cipher material and are worth a look. The volume's catalogue record was not matched (Ashley's 1612 'Book of magical charms' is a separate digital record, not shown to be this volume). Not on DECODE; known.py no hit for Case MS 5017.
why: Shows a 17th-century amateur cipher alphabet inside an occult manuscript; useful as a key for any unread characters elsewhere in the volume.
verify: View nby_dig/2714 and neighbouring pages (2764); check whether any longer passage in the volume is in these characters.
